findings.issue: The HJ raise-and-calls justification describes a spot that can't happen, and the range was built on the same wrong idea. It says 'the raiser came from an early seat and is strong'. But HJ sits directly after UTG, so on the first round no call can come between a UTG raise and HJ. HJ only faces raise-and-calls after limping itself, when a later seat (CO, BTN, SB or BB) raised and others called. The acceptance script builds exactly this: 4 call, 5 call, 6 raise, 1 call, 2 fold, 3 fold, 4 call, then hero 5. This text is strategy the user sees (SPEC-15 requires each justification to explain the range correctly). The grid follows the wrong idea too: HJ raise-and-calls folds A9s-A6s, KTs, QTs and 87s, which CO raise-and-calls calls. Yet HJ already has a bet in, faces a wider raiser from a later seat, and the betting is close to closed, so it should be at least as wide as CO.
findings.evidence: Spec section 5 rule 3, plus the SCRIPTS entry for HJ raise-and-calls in tests/advice/preflop.acceptance.test.ts. Compare the HJ and CO raise-and-calls grids, row A and row K.
findings.fix: Rewrite the HJ raise-and-calls justification for the spot that actually occurs: we limped, a later seat raised, at least one player called, and we owe one more bet into a multiway pot, usually closing the action. Then review the grid against that premise, for example by calling the suited aces and suited kings that CO raise-and-calls calls. Keep it within the 6-18% band.

findings.issue: In BB blind-defence, K9o is C*/F (a borderline call) while the weaker Q9o, J9o and T9o are plain C. K8o and Q8o are both F*/C. Marking the strongest x9o as the edge-of-range hand, with weaker hands of the same shape called outright, is a small inversion. Golden spots and grading will treat K9o as the close decision.
findings.evidence: BB blind-defence grid, row 9 (index 5): 'C C*/F C C C R*/C ...'
findings.fix: Mark K9o as a plain C. If an x9o hand belongs at the edge, use the weakest unconnected one instead. Alternatively, explain in the justification why K9o is the edge hand.

findings.issue: A-9 says a word is a run of letters, but no test checks that rule. The mutant that changes /\p{L}+/gu to /\S+/ in wordCount (src/advice/preflop-chart.ts) passes every test, so a justification of 50 numbers or punctuation tokens would be accepted.
findings.evidence: Mutation run in a scratch copy: [words-any] 13 passed.
findings.fix: Add a case such as justification: Array(60).fill('1').join(' ') or '- '.repeat(60). Expect the missing-justification problem.

findings.issue: chartCell has an extra error path, RangeError('Unknown hand class <hc>'), that is not in the spec's error list. It is reasonable because HandClass is a plain string, but it is unrequested behaviour.
findings.evidence: Spec section 5 'Error handling' lists only the missing-spot message for chartCell.
findings.fix: Keep it and record it in the build log as a deliberate guard, or drop it and let the lookup return undefined. The first is preferred.

findings.issue: In positionOf, 'start <= 0 ? seats : rotate' treats start === 0 as a special case it doesn't need: rotating at 0 gives the same array. The mutant that changes it to '< 0' survives because the two are equivalent.
findings.evidence: Mutation run: [start-lt0] passes. The result is identical.
findings.fix: Optional: use 'start < 0' (or 'start === -1') so the condition reads as 'no seat after the button, so wrap around'.

summary: The code matches the spec. Position rotation (including gapped seats), situation classification (own limp ignored, limps before a raise not counted as callers, blinds facing one raise are blind-defence, two or more raises are re-raise), legalisation (capped or no raise gives call, nothing owed gives check for call and fold, the alternative is adjusted the same way and nulled when equal) and move lookup all match section 5. The validator emits every listed message exactly, in file order. I ran 26 mutants against preflop.ts and preflop-chart.ts. The tests killed all of them except two that behave identically to the original (start<=0 vs <0; the hero's own limp with no raise, which can't occur) and one real gap: the letters-only word count. The chart is mostly coherent poker: the unopened ranges nest, there are no raise/fold inversions across tighter and looser spots, and the justifications read as original and match their grids. The exception is HJ raise-and-calls. Its justification and its tight grid assume an early raiser, but the spot only arises after HJ's own limp with a later raiser (MAJOR, SPEC-15). I did not read build-log.md (per the rules), so the SPEC-15 build-log note is unverified here.
